author: official
summary: Counts down to a deadline in the visitor’s browser — typed on the element, or read from a calendar’s events feed, paging through what’s next — as plain digits or split-flap cards, and hides or swaps itself when nothing is left.

attributes.name: data-deadline
attributes.description: ISO date-time WITH an explicit offset (Z or ±hh:mm) naming a real date; otherwise the root is left as authored. With data-src it is the fallback, used when the feed gives no event to show.

attributes.name: data-src
attributes.description: An events feed URL (the events coral’s feed for one public calendar). The root makes one GET to it on load and shows the events still to come in what’s-next order: each counts to its start while that is ahead and to its end once it is under way, and at zero carries on to the next without a reload. The calendar’s own time zone places its all-day events; nothing about time is written on the page. Without data-src the root makes no network call.

attributes.name: data-event
attributes.description: With data-src, on a child element: its text becomes that part of the event being shown (emptied when the event has none). when is the date or range in the page’s language — an all-day event’s dates as the calendar wrote them, a timed event in the visitor’s zone with the zone named. location is the place, or a URL without its scheme. calendar is the calendar’s name. position is like 2/4, empty for a single event.

attributes.name: data-event-href
attributes.description: With data-src, on a child link: its href (removed when there is none). location is the location itself when the whole field is an http(s) URL and otherwise the platform’s map for the place; url is the event’s own URL; add is an add-to-calendar link for the event. Only http(s), a map, or that add link is ever written.

attributes.name: data-event-if
attributes.description: With data-src, on a child element: shown only while that holds for the event being shown, hidden otherwise. url and place are the two kinds of location; several is true when there is more than one event to page through.

attributes.name: data-event-nav
attributes.description: With data-src, on a child button: pages to the previous or next event. Disabled at the first and the last; it does not wrap.

attributes.name: data-event-fit
attributes.description: With data-src, on the root or one child: that element is kept at least as tall as the tallest event needs, measured again when its width changes, so paging moves nothing around it.

attributes.name: data-event-more
attributes.description: With data-src, on a child element whose text the host’s CSS clips (a two-line description): when the text really is clipped the element gets data-event-clipped and becomes a control (role, tabindex, aria-expanded; click, Enter, Space) that toggles data-event-open, for which the host’s CSS shows the whole text. Text that fits is left exactly as authored. Showing another event closes it.

attributes.name: data-event-clipped
attributes.description: Written by the coral, not by the host: present on a data-event-more element while its text is clipped. The hook for showing that there is more (an arrow, a cursor).

attributes.name: data-event-open
attributes.description: Written by the coral, not by the host: present on a data-event-more element while the visitor has opened it. The host’s CSS shows the whole text for it.

attributes.name: data-unit
attributes.description: With data-src, on a child element: its text becomes the page-language word for that unit, from the browser (日, hr, Tg.). Left as authored where the browser has none.

attributes.name: data-expired
attributes.description: What the root does when nothing is left to count to (the deadline, or the last event of a feed): hide it, or replace its content with data-expired-text (text without a data-expired-text hides).

attributes.name: data-expired-text
attributes.description: Text shown in place of the countdown when data-expired is text.

attributes.name: data-part
attributes.description: On a child element: which unit it shows, two digits minimum and as many as needed (no upper bound). The largest unit present also carries every unit above it (hours alone show 53 for 2 d 5 h).

attributes.name: data-flip
attributes.description: On a data-part element: show one split-flap card per digit instead of plain text. data-flip="false" keeps plain text.

attributes.name: data-flip-faces
attributes.description: On a data-flip element: comma-separated faces its cards can show. Every card is locked to the widest of them. It only sizes the cards: with data-flip-mode="drum" the wheel is still 9, 8, … 0, so the default written out behaves exactly like leaving it out.

attributes.name: data-flip-mode
attributes.description: On a data-flip element: drum makes each card a counter wheel that only turns forward (always 9, 8, … 0), folding through every digit in between — the tens of the seconds go 0→9→8→7→6→5 at the minute. Unset keeps the straight-to-target flip. Reduced motion always goes straight.
